transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2028-04-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: 49 minutes
Conference link: zoom.us/j/xxxxxxxx
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, James Ho, Lena Park (Redwood); Priya Natarajan, Ethan Cole, Maya Leung, Carlos Ruiz (AnchorPoint)

Summary:
- Kickoff for 4-week success sprint: staging access, security review, pilot metrics defined.
- Quick alignment on network/provisioning owners and security checklist (SAML, KMS, audit logs).
- Agreed next steps: runbook share, staging VPC, follow-up deep-dive on batch/cache.

Topics covered:
- Staging environment and service account access
- Data residency / encryption / KMS integration
- Model routing, batching, and KV cache considerations for low-latency use cases
- Pilot success criteria and SLOs (p99 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens)
- Rollout timeline and checkpoints

Action items (captured above): see metadata action_items list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. i know we've got a packed 45, 50 minute window so i'll kick off quick intros. i'm sofia, i'm your AE and i'll be coordinating the sprint.
[00:12] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): hi, priya here - head of ml ops. super excited to get this going. we've got ethan and maya on from infra and security.
[00:20] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): morning all, ethan. platform eng. i'll own the vpc/network side.
[00:25] James Ho (Redwood): james from customer success, i'll be your weekly sync person.
[00:30] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): maya, security lead - i'll be following the compliance items and the SAML/KMS bits.
[00:35] Lena Park (Redwood): lena, solutions eng. i'll take the technical deep dive later. a lot to cover but we'll triage.
[00:40] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): awesome. quick agenda: share runbook, confirm staging access plan, talk security/priorities, then technical follow-up scheduling. sound good?
[00:49] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): sounds good. also timeline — we're aiming to have a pilot with 2 models in staging in 3 weeks, so any blockers early would be great to surface.
[01:02] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): perfect. that's inline with our standard 4-week sprint. first, access: ethan, can you confirm if you can create a staging VPC and a service account we can use, or do you prefer us to provide an IP allowlist for hosted callbacks?
[01:20] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): we can do a staging VPC and add a service account. easier for us to centralize access that way. i'll need the service account email and the minimal IAM roles.
[01:33] Lena Park (Redwood): we'll provide a minimal least-privilege role: read/write to the model artifacts bucket for staging, and network egress only to Redwood collector endpoints. i'll send the exact IAM JSON. note that if you want private deployment later we'll switch to VPC peering but for now service account is fine.
[01:50] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): on encryption: do you support customer-managed keys? we need to show this to compliance.
[01:58] James Ho (Redwood): yes, we support KMS integration both in hosted and private modes. for hosted we'll show KMS binding for customer artifacts; for private we can integrate HSM later. i'll attach the security brief.
[02:12] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): cool; also audit logs — we need per-call traceability for two months.
[02:20] Lena Park (Redwood): we have token-level tracing and per-route logs, retention is configurable up to 12 months as an add-on. by default it's 30 days; we'll note the options in the runbook.
[02:35] Carlos Ruiz (AnchorPoint): quick Q: latency targets — our engineering OKR is p99 inference under 300ms for 512 tokens. is that realistic on the hosted plan?
[02:46] Lena Park (Redwood): depends on model and concurrency. for medium-sized models we typically hit p99 around 200-350ms with our dedicated pools. hosted can be burstier; for consistent p99 we'd recommend a dedicated or reserved capacity profile. i can run a quick mapping based on your expected RPS.
[03:04] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): our expected workload for pilot is ~15 rps, peaks to 40. cost's also a concern — we need to balance latency vs unit cost.
[03:15] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): totally. part of the sprint we'll run a small benchmark in staging with your sample prompts so we can recommend batching and quantization profiles to hit target SLOs while keeping cost down.
[03:30] Speaker 3: (unlabeled) sorry quick interjection, are there any limitations on prompt size for prefix caching?
[03:38] Lena Park (Redwood): good question — our prefix/KV cache has limits per entry, and effectiveness depends on repetition in the workload. i'll demo prefix caching patterns in the deep-dive; in general, smaller stable prefixes get big gains.
[03:52] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): on SAML: we have Okta. what's the SR flow to try SSO in staging?
[03:59] James Ho (Redwood): we have a SAML guide for Okta, we'll need a test idp config and a metadata file. we can spin up a test account for you and walk through the flow. note that for initial pilot you can do email-based invites too.
[04:12] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): good to know. procurement compliance will ask for SOC 2 and ISO docs — can you send those?
[04:19] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): yes, i'll attach our compliance pack. we'll also share the SOC 2 attestation and networking diagrams.
[04:28] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): regarding data retention — in staging we'll send only synthetic PII-free data but for production we'll need data residency in eu-west for GDPR reasons. does Redwood support region pinning?
[04:40] Lena Park (Redwood): yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we have EU regions as well but if residency is strict, Dedicated or Private is the recommended path.
[04:52] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): ok. next, can we talk about alerting? we want to be notified on error spikes and latency degradations.
[04:59] James Ho (Redwood): the console supports per-route alerts and webhook integrations. we'll set up an alerting template for the pilot and include runbook triggers for incident ops.
[05:12] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): timeline recap — what are the milestones for the next 4 weeks?
[05:18] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): week 0 (this week): access, runbook, staging VPC. week 1: initial integration and smoke tests. week 2: benchmark + tuning (batching, quant). week 3: pilot evaluation and handoff doc for production.
[05:33] Carlos Ruiz (AnchorPoint): who will be the single technical point of contact from redwood during the sprint?
[05:38] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): lena will be the SE lead for technical tasks and james will do overall CS cadence. lena's contact is lena@redwood.ai.
[05:45] Lena Park (Redwood): i'll also set up a shared slack channel for faster debugging.
[05:50] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): perfect. about credentials — can we do temporary keys or do you need long-lived service accounts?
[05:57] Lena Park (Redwood): temporary short-lived tokens are fine. we can use workload identity federation if you prefer no long-lived keys. i'll include both options in the IAM doc.
[06:08] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): can we run a quick check on firewall rules? our security team is particular about egress endpoints.
[06:14] James Ho (Redwood): we'll provide a concise allowlist with both hostnames and CIDR ranges; we also support TLS-only egress and mutual TLS for Private deployments.
[06:26] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): okay, sounds good. i want to flag an internal constraint: procurement needs a SOW and SLA summary before the 2nd week. can you provide a draft?
[06:36] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): yes i can draft SOW+SLA and share by next tuesday.
[06:41] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): thanks.
[06:45] Lena Park (Redwood): moving into technical specifics quickly — for the benchmark i'll need 10 representative prompts and a sample embedding/response payload. priya, can you share those?
[06:55] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): yes i'll compile and drop into the shared folder by EOD tomorrow.
[07:02] Carlos Ruiz (AnchorPoint): one more — do you have guidance on tokenization differences between model variants? we've seen output length differ and it skews cost.
[07:12] Lena Park (Redwood): noted — we'll include a tokenization worksheet and a quick script to normalize token counts between models. that'll help compare cost per 1k tokens accurately.
[07:24] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): regarding canary policy, we may want A/B between quantized and full fp16 models. any gotchas?
[07:32] Lena Park (Redwood): quantization can introduce small quality regressions; we'll run your evaluation prompts through both and give a regression report. our optimize tool flags regressions tied to prompt sets.
[07:45] Speaker 2: (unlabeled) sorry, do we have any limits on concurrent KV cache entries?
[07:50] Lena Park (Redwood): there's soft limits based on instance memory; for heavy KV cache use, we recommend dedicated pools with larger memory configs. we'll surface recommended instance sizes in the tuning guide.
[08:03] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): ok great. quick logistics — what's the best way to escalate if we hit a blocker?
[08:10] James Ho (Redwood): for severity 1 production-impacting issues you have the support SN ticket and a pager rotation; during the pilot you're routed to the on-call SE. we'll add our on-call contact to the runbook.
[08:21] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): can we also have an export of trace logs for audits?
[08:26] Lena Park (Redwood): yes, logs can be exported to your logging bucket or to a SIEM via webhook. i'll include export options.
[08:36] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): ok wrapping up — quick recap and owners. redwood will: send runbook + IAM doc (sofia/lena), provide compliance pack (sofia), prepare a short benchmark plan (lena). anchorpoint will: provision staging VPC (ethan), share prompts (priya), provision test SAML user (maya).
[08:57] Priya Natarajan (AnchorPoint): that matches our notes. can we lock a time for the deep technical walkthrough next week?
[09:05] Lena Park (Redwood): yes i'm available 2028-04-20 0900-1100 PDT - i'll send a calendar invite.
[09:13] Carlos Ruiz (AnchorPoint): fine with me.
[09:16] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): great. any final questions?
[09:20] Ethan Cole (AnchorPoint): none from me.
[09:22] Maya Leung (AnchorPoint): nope.
[09:24] Sofia Martinez (Redwood): thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a slack channel. talk soon.
[09:30] END OF TRANSCRIPT

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had a few speaker attribution swaps and mis-heard acronyms (e.g., K V cache transcribed as "K V cache" or "KV cash"), we've left those as-is to reflect raw export.
